items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...from Al Jays. [INTERVIEWEE] Frankie Dutton. Mm-hm. They never did read. Buddy Dutton. Buddy Dutton. But he read.

ctx.x: No, he was head, yeah he's a head man. Yeah, all. Yeah. You know, just know them how they read music. But Poissy and his brother. Now, them fellas there used to be, now all, most of all Jack Carey, band always, break time. All by the people, so. Louie, Louie Nelson. Did you ever hear this name? Yeah, I heard him. Yeah? He wasn't reading then. No. Never did read, huh?
No, no. Never did read, huh? No, no, never did read. And there were, the fella playing the trombone, what do you call them again, from Al Jays.

Frankie Dutton. Mm-hm. They never did read. Buddy Dutton. Buddy Dutton. But he read. Yeah, you know Yank's dear brother. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. But he read, he read musicals. He used to play that band over the roof before Allen. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. because he used to play that band over the roof, before Allen made up his band.

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: When I got big enough, you can call him Al Jays, when I got big enough, he cut Willie Jones right here on this corner.

ctx.x: His mother named Elizabeth. That's right.

And he lived over here, then he come over here afterwards. Then he come over here and right here. When I got big enough, you can call him Al Jays, when I got big enough, he cut Willie Jones right here on this corner. Yeah, 12 little fella.
Were there many other bands over there that played dances, like Buddy Johnson had a band I guess, and Deucin, any others over there much you can remember? Peter Boccage, I guess he had one at times.
